I'm noting the future dates and checking version compatibility — Next 16.4, React 19.3, Tailwind 4, and Prisma 7's new driver adapter requirement add complexity, while TypeScript 7's native Go port could introduce compatibility risks with Next.js. Now I'm weighing database options to keep the overall risk low.

I could lean on Node's built-in `node:sqlite` to skip native dependencies and an ORM entirely, though I'm unsure how well it plays with Next's bundling and Vercel's ephemeral filesystem given the PRD calls for PostgreSQL/Supabase — so an abstracted data access layer feels safer for portability. Prisma would make that Postgres switch easy, but Prisma 7's SQLite setup needs the better-sqlite3 adapter plus its new config format, and I'm not fully confident on those exact API details, which pushes me to also consider Drizzle ORM with better-sqlite3 or Postgres as an alternative.

If that fails there's always `serverExternalPackages` or a dynamic require via `createRequire` as a fallback.

Given the PRD wants Vercel + PostgreSQL deployability, I'll build a repository layer under `src/lib/db` so swapping to Postgres later stays localized, and I'll explain the dependency choice in the plan since the guidelines ask me to justify new dependencies before using them—then proceed since the user said to go ahead directly. Let me weigh whether Prisma fits better here.

Prisma 7 dropped the Rust engine for a TS query compiler plus driver adapters, which still means native binary downloads unless I use something like better-sqlite3 or node:sqlite directly. Prisma 6 is more familiar and stable, works out of the box with SQLite by downloading its query engine binary, and makes switching to Postgres later as simple as changing the provider and connection string—that lines up well with the PRD's PostgreSQL/Supabase direction.

I'm weighing node:sqlite's zero-install-risk simplicity against Prisma 6's maturity and type safety, and leaning toward Prisma 6 with SQLite since it's more maintainable and PRD-aligned, just us

"# Rencana Implementasi CodeKids (berdasarkan PRD.md)

## 1. Hasil Analisis Project
- Folder `e:\codekids` **hanya berisi `PRD.md`**: belum ada kode, `package.json`, atau git.
- Jadi **semua fitur PRD belum diimplementasikan**, dan tidak ada fitur lama yang berisiko rusak.
- Lingkungan: Node 24.12, npm 11.6 (harus lewat `npm.cmd` karena PowerShell memblokir `npm.ps1`), registry npm bisa diakses.

## 2. Dependency yang Dipakai dan Kegunaannya

| Dependency | Kegunaan | Dasar di PRD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next`, `react`, `react-dom` | Framework App Router (RSC untuk landing, Client Component untuk editor dan chat) | Tech stack §4.6 |
| `tailwindcss` v4 + `@tailwindcss/postcss` | Styling + *design tokens* (peach/dongker/oranye) via `@theme` (pengganti `tailwind.config` di v4) | §4.6, NFR-UX-01 |
| `typescript` (dikunci ke v5) | Tipe statis; v7 belum aman untuk Next | Pemeliharaan §5.5 |
| `@google/genai` | SDK resmi Gemini (streaming, *safety settings*, *system instruction*), **hanya dipakai di server** | FR-AI-*, FR-AI-S5 |
| `@dnd-kit/core`, `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `@dnd-kit/utilities` | Drag-and-drop yang mendukung **sentuh + mouse + keyboard** | FR-MISI-04, NFR-UX-06 |
| `prisma` + `@prisma/client` (v6) | ORM relasional. Lokal memakai SQLite (tanpa server DB); untuk produksi cukup ganti `provider` ke PostgreSQL/Supabase | §4.6 Data |
| `bcryptjs` | Hash kata sandi orang tua/guru dan PIN anak | NFR-SC-03 |

To force actual conditional logic rather than a trivial fixed sequence, I'm deciding that performing an action on the wrong cell type (picking where there's no fruit, watering where there's no pot/seedling) should trigger a friendly error and stop execution — otherwise a simple "repeat N [forward, pick, water]" program would always succeed without needing "if" logic. 18: With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) enabled, a session read happens at request time, so it can't be prerendered into the static shell. Authenticated UI streams in behind a `<Suspense>` boundary instead, and data derived from the session can still be cached.

For a complete, runnable version, see the [with-iron-session-cache-components example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-iron-session-cache-components).

296: Two things keep it that way:
297: 
298: - If you tune the lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife), keep `stale` at 30 seconds or more. Below that, the scope drops out of prefetching. See [`cacheLife` client cache behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#client-cache-behavior).
299: - A route that _also_ depends on the URL (a `params` or `searchParams` value) needs [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) on the links pointing at it. That opts into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link data ahead of the click.
300: 
301: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
302: <Link href={`/notes/${note.id}`} prefetch={true}>
303:   {note.text}
304: </Link>
305: ```
306: 
307: The destination needs [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for this, so enable the [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag or set `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. Add the prop where the wait is worth it: that prefetch costs one server invocation per link, so a sidebar of `/chat/[id]` links pays that cost per item.

309: ## Common pitfalls
310: 
311: - **Reading `cookies()` or `headers()` inside a plain `use cache` function.** This throws. Read the request outside and pass the value in, or use `use cache: private`.
312: - **Putting secrets or personal data in cache keys or tags.** Arguments and `cacheTag` values are stored in plain text. Key and tag on a stable identifier, not on sensitive input.
313: - **Trusting the client for authorization.** UI checks hide elements, but they don't protect data. Re-verify the session in every Server Action and [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), close to the data. See [Authorization](/docs/app/guides/authentication#authorization).

15: The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.
16: 
17: Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.
18: 
19: When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

154: ## Known issue: shared cookie across projects
155: 
156: The DevTools use a `next-instant-navigation-testing` cookie to hold back dynamic content and freeze the page at the instant UI. Because cookies are scoped to the domain and not the port, running multiple projects on the same domain (typically `localhost`) means the cookie is shared across them and can cause unexpected behavior. Clear the cookie or close the Navigation Inspector panel when switching between projects to avoid issues.
